In-sample classification statistics

Source: R/methods.R
psp_classification.Rd

Compares posterior mean outcome probabilities (predict(type = "prob")) with the observed outcomes (missing outcomes are left out).

Usage

psp_classification(fit, draws = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A fitted psprobit object.

draws

Number of posterior draws used for the probabilities.

Value

A list with hit_rate (share of observations whose most probable outcome is the observed one), auc (binary models: area under the ROC curve; NA for ordered models), brier (mean squared error of the probability vector) and confusion (observed by predicted table).

Examples

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(4, 4), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 3, beta = c(0, 1), rho = 0.4, seed = 2)
fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1, data = d, index = c("id", "time"), W = W, impacts = FALSE,
                control = psp_control(iter = 200, warmup = 100, chains = 1, seed = 2))
#> Warning: Possible convergence problems (R-hat > 1.01 or bulk ESS < 100) for: (Intercept), x1, rho, sigma_alpha. Consider more iterations.
psp_classification(fit, draws = 50)
#> $hit_rate
#> [1] 0.6041667
#> 
#> $auc
#> [1] 0.6381119
#> 
#> $brier
#> [1] 0.2349346
#> 
#> $confusion
#>         predicted
#> observed  0  1
#>        0 20  6
#>        1 13  9
#>
